title: Grove's Ethena integration only grants an approval on-chain; the mint or redeem is executed off-contract by Ethena
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.10.3 is explicit that `prepareUSDeMint` exists to approve "the Ethena minter to spend USDC from the Grove ALM Proxy so that USDe can be minted. **The actual mint is executed off-contract by Ethena against this approval.**" A...10.4 says the same for `prepareUSDeBurn` and redemption.

This breaks the pattern used everywhere else in the Liquidity Layer, where the controller both authorises and executes in one transaction and then verifies the result by balance delta. Here Grove cannot verify anything: the function returns after `ERC20Lib.approve(proxy, usdc, ethenaMinter, usdcAmount)` (A...10.3.3), and settlement happens later, off-chain, at a price Grove's code never sees.

The accounting consequence is that `LIMIT_USDE_MINT` is decreased at approval time (A...10.3.2). The limit therefore meters **how much Grove has made spendable**, not how much was actually minted. If Ethena fills less than the approval, the limit has still been consumed; the difference reappears only as a residual allowance.

What makes the design acceptable is that the counterparty is a permissioned minter with its own order-signing flow, so a purely on-chain execution path does not exist. But it means the strongest guarantees Grove offers elsewhere — measured output, enforced minimum, post-hoc slippage check — are structurally unavailable for this integration.
description: prepareUSDeMint and prepareUSDeBurn set an allowance and stop, so Grove's rate limit governs authorised exposure rather than realised exposure and cannot observe the eventual fill.
